repeat.message:
Judge the committed results of both contestant roles for this task:

{{task}}

Use only their generated refs and captured base from the core workspace context, with read-only Git from your own managed tree. Determine the next round from your last committed .compete/judged-round.md (none means round 1). Read `git show <contestant-ref>:.compete/result.md` at each supplied contestant ref; both must record this round, and both refs must contain the completed implementation commits beyond the captured base. If a ref, commit or current-round result is missing, report what is missing and ask; do not score stale work, guess a sibling directory, or use an uncommitted file.

Judge them blind: call them Version A and Version B in a random order, and do not look at which is which until you have scored. Score each from 0 to 100 for how well it does what was asked, its design and its code. Write distinct .compete/feedback-a.md and .compete/feedback-b.md in your own tree; each begins `Round: N`, identifies the reviewed contestant commit and says what to improve. Write .compete/judged-round.md with this round and the scores. Commit all three files on your own generated branch before ending your turn or emitting a verdict. Contestants read that feedback commit through the shared Git object database, never by reading your checkout or the main checkout. If one version is clearly better, say WINNER on a line of its own.

queue.message: Report the winning role, ref and reason for review, using the committed scores across the rounds if there is no clear winner. Include the reviewed commit id and Judge’s feedback commit. Do not merge or modify the picked checkout; the user’s later merge is the integration step.
